newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian court sets new term in Credit Bank trial.
newsitem.headline: Romanian court sets new term in Credit Bank trial.

text.p: A Romanian court on Monday postponed a ruling on the troubled private Credit Bank's legal challenge to a central bank (BNR) decision asking a judge to start reorganisation and liquidation procedures.
Bucharest's commercial court set the next hearing for November 8, after a Credit Bank lawyer failed to appear on health grounds, the independent news agency Mediafax said.
In July, the BNR cut financial aid to Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA and another private bank Dacia Felix SA, saying further support might fuel "uncontrollable inflationary pressure".

Immediately after the BNR cut support to Credit Bank, the private bank's present boss, Emil Cioflan, attacked the central bank's move, saying it had harmed the bank's image and affected depositors' confidence.
The BNR move came after a year of continuous state support to the two medium-sized commercial banks to keep them afloat.
Since the 1989 fall of communism not a single bank has been declared bankrupt in Romania.

Credit Bank was rocked by a management crisis after its president Marcel Ivan was arrested on fraud charges in January 1995. It was under special surveillance for several months and has since changed its management teams three times.
Earlier this month Romania's parliament passed a draft law allowing BNR to give credits to two troubled private banks to help them redeem small depositors.

Dacia Felix ran into trouble last November with reports of bad loans of $200 million and a 1995 loss of 642.2 billion lei. A court in the Transylvanian city of Cluj has yet to decide on its reorganisation or winding up. ($=3,306 lei) -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
